themes_detail.label: Animal waste crisis
themes_detail.summary: Unsanitary animal conditions on private property spiked to 3 complaints THIS WEEK versus 0.4 weekly average—a 700% increase (z-score: 5.42)—suggesting a sudden pest or animal control problem emerged in Midwood this week.
evidence: 3 complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.4 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (700% spike, z-score 5.42)
Highest recency signal in dataset—emerged within last 7 days
Unsanitary Animal Private Property is narrow complaint category, suggesting concentrated/acute issue rather than baseline condition
reporting_angles: Are residents reporting a specific location or animal population (rodents, stray dogs, etc.)? Interview 311 complainants.
What is DOHMH or Animal Care doing in response? Has a health risk been identified?

themes_detail.label: Abandoned bikes pile-up
themes_detail.summary: Abandoned bike complaints hit 6 THIS WEEK, up 586% from 0.9 weekly average (z-score: 4.87), indicating either a sudden dumping incident or systemic failure in bike removal.
evidence: 6 complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.9 weekly average (586% spike, z-score 4.87)
Emerged within last 7 days—newest spike after animal waste issue
Suggests concentration in specific area(s) rather than distributed problem
reporting_angles: Map where the abandoned bikes are concentrated—are they near Coney Island Ave or Nostrand Ave corridors where rezoning activity is active?
Interview NYPD and Sanitation; are they aware of a dumping site or are they backlogged on bike removal?

themes_detail.label: Street infrastructure decay
themes_detail.summary: Damaged street signs spiked to 10 complaints last week, up 789% from 1.1 weekly average (z-score: 6.51), and overgrown trees/branches hit 15 complaints (243% spike), signaling accelerating public realm neglect over the last 1-2 weeks.
evidence: Street Sign - Damaged: 10 complaints last week vs. 1.1 weekly average (789% spike, z-score 6.51)
Overgrown Tree/Branches: 15 complaints last week vs. 4.4 weekly average (243% spike, z-score 3.76)
Two infrastructure categories spiking simultaneously over the last 1-2 weeks suggests broader maintenance failure
reporting_angles: Did NYC Parks or DOT face budget cuts, staffing reductions, or equipment failures in the past 2 weeks? Request recent maintenance logs.
Interview residents on specific streets (Coney Island Ave, Ocean Parkway, Nostrand Ave) about visibility hazards and safety concerns from broken signs and overgrown branches.

themes_detail.label: Litter basket shortage
themes_detail.summary: Litter basket requests jumped to 6 complaints last week, up 433% from 1.1 weekly average (z-score: 8.13), indicating either residents perceive inadequate street sanitation infrastructure or baskets are being removed/damaged.
evidence: Litter Basket Request: 6 complaints last week vs. 1.1 weekly average (433% spike, z-score 8.13)
High z-score indicates statistically exceptional deviation
Aligns thematically with overgrown trees and street sign decay—points to broader sanitation/maintenance gap
reporting_angles: Has DSNY reduced basket deployment or collection frequency in Midwood in recent weeks? Request service schedules.
Map complaint locations to see if baskets are concentrated in specific commercial corridors (Coney Island Ave, Avenue M, Nostrand Ave) where foot traffic is high.

themes_detail.label: Cannabis retail expansion debate
themes_detail.summary: Cannabis retailer complaints rose to 4 last week, up 191% from 1.4 weekly average (z-score: 3.06), suggesting resident pushback as the City's retail licensing program accelerates in this neighborhood.
evidence: Cannabis Retailer complaints: 4 last week vs. 1.4 weekly average (191% spike, z-score 3.06)
Spike emerged in the last 1-2 weeks as retail licensing accelerates citywide
Reflects emerging community tension, not baseline issue
reporting_angles: How many cannabis retail licenses have been issued or are pending in CD 314? Interview local residents and merchants about concerns (youth access, odor, loitering).
Are any community board members or elected officials considering stricter local restrictions? Check CB meeting minutes and council member statements.
